Bradley Ochoa’s knowledge state in Scenario 4 includes what he personally does, says, and hears: he has prepared an integrated presentation draft, he tells Katherine he is excited about its potential, and he explicitly says he is “convinced that this integrated approach will set us apart from our competitors.” Katherine also tells him the draft looks comprehensive and well thought out.

Bradley does not know future outcomes at this point: whether the board will approve the presentation, whether competitors will actually respond negatively, or whether the integrated strategy will ultimately succeed in the market. He also has not yet expressed the later Scenario 5 belief about personal and professional growth.

In Scenario 4, the belief Bradley explicitly states is that the integrated approach will succeed and set them apart from competitors. This matches choice a.

ANSWER: a
